terms.meaning: a short code, such as 1M for one month, that the store uses to pick a time range
a shared place where the app keeps data that many screens read and update

sections.name: File setup, periods
sections.title: Imports and time range list
sections.what: Loads the layout pieces, icons, navigation, theme, shared UI parts and the analytics store. Also lists the five time ranges: 7 days, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months and 1 year.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list gives the user a choice of ranges the store can supply. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The period codes must match the keys the analytics store expects, or the screen cannot request data for them.

sections.name: AnalyticsScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Header, period picker and health score
sections.what: Draws the top of the Analytics page: a back button, the title, a row of time period buttons, and a Health Score ring with three bars for Medicine, Lab Results and Activity. It asks the store to load the dashboard when the page opens, and shows a spinner until adherence data arrives.
sections.why: Likely reason: the health score is the first thing a user should see, so it sits at the top with its three parts beside it. The fetch on open is likely there so the numbers are current each time the page opens.
sections.watch_out: The spinner only checks the adherence data, so other numbers may show as dashes while the page looks finished.

sections.name: AnalyticsScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Medicine adherence card
sections.what: Shows the medicine adherence percentage, a bar chart of the last 14 days where days at 80 percent or more are bright and others are faded, and counts of taken, skipped and missed doses.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick visual check of whether medicines are being taken on time.
sections.watch_out: Missing data shows as zero or dashes, so a real zero and missing data look alike.

sections.name: AnalyticsScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Health trends grid
sections.what: Shows one card for each tracked lab measure, with its latest value, unit, a status badge, a small bar chart of recent readings coloured by status, and an arrow with the change from the previous period.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a user see at a glance which lab values are moving and whether they are in range.
sections.watch_out: The trend colour depends only on whether the change text starts with a plus sign, so a rise is always shown in the warning colour even when a rise is good for that measure.

sections.name: AnalyticsScreen (part 4)
sections.title: Water intake chart
sections.what: Shows the last 10 days of water intake as labelled bars in litres, plus a row with the daily average, how many days reached the goal, and the best day. Days at or above 2.5 litres use full colour; other days are faded.
sections.why: Likely reason: a daily hydration goal of 2.5 litres is built into this screen to show progress.
sections.watch_out: The 2.5 litre goal and the 3.5 litre bar scale are fixed in this file, not read from user settings.

sections.name: AnalyticsScreen (part 5)
sections.title: Sleep quality chart
sections.what: Shows the last 10 nights of sleep hours as bars, with the average, best and worst night. Nights with at least 7 hours use full colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: 7 hours is treated as the healthy sleep line for this screen.
sections.watch_out: The 7 hour line and the 10 hour bar scale are fixed in code, so changing the target means editing this file.

sections.name: BreakdownRow (part 1)
sections.title: Reusable sub-score row
sections.what: A small reusable row that shows one sub-score such as Medicine: a coloured dot, the label, a thin bar filled to the score, and the percentage number.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same layout is needed three times in the score area, so it is written once.
sections.watch_out: The bar width is set directly from the value, so a number above 100 or below 0 would overflow or disappear.

sections.name: BreakdownRow (part 2)
sections.title: Styles for the Analytics page
sections.what: Holds the look settings for the page and the sub-score row: colours, sizes, spacing and layout. Changing a value here changes how things look, not what data is shown.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps look settings in one place at the bottom of the file.
sections.watch_out: Some colours and sizes are typed in directly rather than taken from the shared theme, so a theme change may miss them.
